rv.q: The Old Man & the Pool is one helluva sandwich.
Funny thing is, you never want him to shut up.
Catching up with him at regular intervals, we are watching the construction of a lifelong narrative arc.
In generously detailing the less-than-ideal fragments of his life, he reveals the many reasons we should keep relishing ours.
Birbiglia has become expert at finding the comedy in catastrophe, and the show builds to a climax that manages to be both hilarious and genuinely moving.
The latest Mike check-up, the funny and endearing The Old Man & the Pool, dives back into questions of life and death, delivered with a goofy gallows grin that helps the medicine go down.
The version we do have is gratifying.
You may not pee in the pool at the Beaumont, but I can't guarantee you won't pee in your pants.
In that respect, The Old Man and the Pool is Birbiglia at his most truthful.
Birbiglia is excellent at his craft, knowing when to guide the audience through an emotion and when to perfectly execute a gag that has slowly been building.
Somehow, Birbiglia makes the business of death, the business of illness, the business of staying alive, the funniest thing.
So, dive right in! The water’s perfect!
Here’s hoping that Birbiglia continues to come to Broadway each season with new autobiographical monologues and inspires the same kind of turnout.
Birbiglia has crafted a deeply personal and surprisingly moving meditation on mortality, middle age, and the small moments that define our lives.

Birbiglia's latest one-man show is a meditation on mortality, middle age, and the small moments that make life worth living, delivered with his trademark self-deprecating humor and masterful storytelling.
When you’re in the good company of Birbiglia, after all, it feels perfectly normal to laugh in the face of death.
He’s brought his latest show, the terrific The Old Man & the Pool, to the Vivian Beaumont.
Birbiglia is totally on brand in his largely delightful solo show, The Old Man and the Pool.
But it certainly demonstrates, if we needed any more proof, that at a Birbiglia show, it’s hard to stop laughing.

His latest solo work, which opens tonight at Theater and runs through January 15, is diverting and occasionally hilarious, but ultimately feels a bit tossed-off, an agreeable but flimsy set which washes over you nicely but leaves little lasting impression.
I was thoroughly enraptured by every word of a performance that flew by, and became the most fun I've had at a show in years, if not ever.

cn.t: Birbiglia delivers another masterfully crafted solo show, mining his health scares and mortality fears for both big laughs and genuine emotion through his signature circular storytelling and self-deprecating humor.

vs.sum: The Vivian Beaumont Theater offers exceptional sightlines and sound quality due to its unique thrust stage design, ensuring a great view and auditory experience from nearly every seat. While the ambiance is enhanced by its location within the Lincoln Center, the comfort level is average with some reports of tight seating, and facilities are typical for a Broadway venue.

acc.note: Orchestra accessible via elevator. Induction hearing loop for t-coil. Loge NOT accessible (stairs only).
